what: A screen-sized photo panel pinned to the screen first looks like a picture frame on the background, held in a transparent border 100px thick (50px at 768px and below), then while the panel’s top edge goes from the screen center to the top of the screen, tied straight to scroll, the border melts to 0 and it becomes a full-screen background. In the same span the photo in the panel deepens from sharp (blur 0) to 16px blur and a 40% dark multiply veil covers it, making a base for the text (plan cards) rising over it

options.border-narrow: Initial thickness at 768px and below, default 50
options.radius: Initial corner roundness (css), default 0px — flattens out to 0
options.start · end: ScrollTrigger range, default top center · top top
options.--fx-blur: Photo blur when fully spread, default 16px
options.--fx-shade: Darkness of the dark ink overlay, default 40%
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Blurring photo (child) — without it only the edge melts

use: Plan text

from.where: index.html .rd-plan__bg (PLAN section) — original c(): set border 100 (phone 50) → to opacity 1 · border 0 · borderRadius 0, from img filter blur(0px) (css blur-lg 16px, scale-125), both start top center · end top top · scrub true, after:bg-black/40 mix-blend-multiply

note: Like inset-grow-scrub, a panel opens to fill the screen, but that one opens the clip-path window and scale after the panel top touches the top of the screen, while this one melts the transparent border thickness of a screen-sized panel from when the panel is at screen center and blurs the photo — the start position, blur and no scale differ, so it is kept separate
